forks.decision: External tasks run fully native with a local checkout without upstream history, a local uv venv or Go/Rust toolchain, and our replay of the instance's FAIL_TO_PASS/PASS_TO_PASS tests; no Docker
One evolutionary loop mutates code and text; a candidate is a commit
The loop engine is GEPA optimize_anything with repeat runs on frontier candidates
The loop may mutate only src and prompts; winners land as human-reviewed draft PRs
The judge labels per-task applicability and critiques each rollout for reflection only; grader correctness is the only objective
The Phase 4 power gate is retired; every paid run requires an explicit spend ceiling

contradictions: Minor decisions say the three local hard tasks (rg_search_dispatch, rg_trait_implementors, gin_servehttp_flow) form the cheap tier, which AC-14 runs on every candidate. AC-4 and Approach step 4 put those same tasks into a stratified dev/test split, and nothing pins them to dev. Any of them that lands in test is scored during optimization, which breaks the held-out property AC-16 relies on.

AC-11 says that when judge agreement is below threshold the system 'shall refuse to supply labels or critiques to an optimizer run', so the run proceeds without them. Its test contract (test_low_agreement_blocks_optimizer) instead fails when 'optimizer starts with agreement below threshold', so the test asserts that the optimizer is blocked. The AC and its test specify different behavior.

Approach step 5 orders the applier as commit on a scratch branch, then regenerate AGENTS.md, then rewrite the byte-lock values. AC-13 also lists commit before regen. AGENTS.md is outside the src/** + prompts/** allowlist (AC-13, minor decisions) and has no stated applier exemption. Under that order, the commit that F-2 calls 'the candidate', recorded as git_sha (AC-5) and opened as the draft PR (AC-16), lacks the regen and byte-lock update. That commit fails agents_md_matches_prompt_sources (src/mcp/mod.rs:1229) and server_instructions_byte_lock (:771) in CI.

Approach step 1 says 'a rerun resumes through the baseline store', and AC-9 says to 'leave completed rows reusable'. AC-6 reuses rows only 'WHEN a baseline-arm cell is requested', so after a quota stop the completed candidate and tilth-arm cells are re-bought. Extending reuse to those cells would also be wrong: the run key (entity binding, Approach step 1) has no candidate git_sha or binary_sha256, so one candidate's row would be returned for another.

The entity binding says external tasks 'subclass Task and override check_correctness, as gin_edit_render_context does'. But Task.check_correctness(result_text, repo_path) -> tuple[bool, str] (benchmark/tasks/base.py:143, called at run.py:783) cannot return pass_rate or F2P/P2P counts (AC-2) and never receives the trajectory. The AC-2 and AC-17 test seams are exactly ExternalTask.check_correctness. Task also has no prepare() (AC-1 seam). Neither the Interface sketches nor the crust delta declare a change to the Task ABC or to the run.py call site.
orphaned_decisions: 'Rewrites only the expected values of server_instructions_byte_lock' (Approach step 5, AC-13, minor decisions) never says which values. The lock asserts a length plus starts_with, ends_with, and contains phrases (src/mcp/mod.rs:771-805). Only the length can be derived mechanically. Rewriting the phrase assertions would neutralize guards on section-read and escape guidance; leaving them makes most prompt mutations fail. The spec names cwd_guidance_spans_present and the 2KB cap as retained guards but says nothing on the byte lock's phrase guards. AC-13's test checks only a benchmark/run.py patch, so no test observes where the exemption ends.

AC-15 says the paid tier 'shall compare it against frozen baseline rows', but nothing defines what the comparison produces or what consumes it. F-5 and AC-12 make candidate grader correctness the only score, so the stored baselines never influence selection. The goal's 'optimize against once-run stored baselines' is therefore undecided. AC-15's test covers only the frontier re-run.

'Codex cells run serially against one CODEX_HOME' (Approach step 1, minor decisions) has no AC or test. evolve.py may launch several run.py processes, and research claim 5 says Codex auth.json must not be shared across concurrent jobs.

AC-14 'stop at the first failing stage with score 0': patch apply and just check fail by exit code, but nothing defines what counts as failing the cheap tier or the paid tier, which produce scores. The cascade's gating is undecided.
unsupported_assumptions: That the claude -p stream under OAuth emits total_cost_usd and a detectable usage-limit rejection. The research doc's Gaps list both, plus the usage-limit exit code, as untested (claims 8 and 9 are 'speculating'). AC-7 (cost ceiling) and AC-9 (infra:quota stop) depend on them. The spec's Risks do not mark them [speculating], AC-9's test uses a canned stream, and no preflight checks a live OAuth stream.

That the GEPA reflection LM and the judge can run on subscription-only auth. The spec never says how either is invoked or how 'reflection calls' and 'judge calls' get a cost for AC-7. If either uses an API key, build_runner_env forwards every ANTHROPIC_-prefixed variable into Claude cells (run.py:174, 196-197), so AC-9's ANTHROPIC_API_KEY guard would abort every Claude cell.

That a reflection LM can write a unified diff over src/** that applies, given only the current diff text and AC-12's side information (rows, trajectories, labels, critiques). The reflective dataset contains no source files, and there is neither evidence nor a smoke AC that proposed src_patch values apply.

That 'each tool description' can be a standalone text component. Only tilth_read's description comes from a file (prompts/tools/read.md via include_str!, src/mcp/tools/definitions.rs:4). The rest are inline literals inside serde_json::json! in definitions.rs, which src_patch may also edit. The spec gives no splice or escape mechanism and no AC or test for writing them (AC-13 'write its text components').

That the run key identifies a stock baseline. It omits harness inputs that change the baseline arm: SYSTEM_PROMPT (benchmark/config.py), --strict-file-tools (which swaps the baseline tool list and appends _STRICT_SYSTEM_GUIDANCE, run.py:420-424, 611), experiment-forced --bare setting sources (run.py:619, 1227), and the per-cell --max-budget-usd cap (run.py:605). Baselines run under different harness configs share a key, so G-5 and AC-6 can reuse the wrong rows.

That held-out tests are hidden because they sit 'outside the agent's checkout' (AC-1). Under native execution the agent has Bash, and tilth's trust-absolute posture serves any absolute host path. A src/**-mutated tilth candidate also runs with host filesystem access. AC-17 scans only for upstream fetches. F-5's premise that 'the loop cannot game a score it cannot touch' has no AC or test showing the grader inputs are unreachable.

That gin-gonic__gin-3741 passes native preflight. AC-4 requires listing it, but AC-3 refuses any task that fails native admission. Only the Rust pick has a fallback (tokio-rs__tokio-6724), and research claim 16 warns that host agents lose the image's test environment.
acceptance_gaps: Approach step 3 gates both judge outputs on calibration-set agreement. AC-11 gates only what is supplied to the optimizer, and AC-10 slices the analysis report by applicability labels with no calibration check. G-6's 'decides where structural tools apply' in the report can therefore rest on uncalibrated labels, and no AC or test observes the report-side gate.
